about: The rehearsal's scenes (bin/kuwai-rehearse, docs/design/REHEARSAL.md). Each scene is one panel in one state: `set` puts services in that state ([service, property, value] or [service, "call", function, arguments]) and is undone after the frame. `kind: worst` is data longer than ordinary, where shortening with an ellipsis is the right answer. `seed` are files written into the private home before the shell starts (paths under that home, e.g. ".local/state/kuwai/notifications.json": Notifs keeps its store under HOME, not XDG_STATE_HOME). A string "@now-300s" or "@now+5400000ms" becomes that moment (epoch seconds or milliseconds); "@now-300iso" the same as ISO text. `running` are helpers a service keeps alive: their stand-in stays up silently (the others exit at once, as on a machine where they are missing). `props` are the panel's own properties; "@date:2026-11-18T10:10:00" is that moment. A seed value "copy:tests/ui/fixtures/x.png" copies that repository file instead of writing JSON. `late` are sets (same form as `set`) applied once the panel is up, for a reading a helper the panel starts would overwrite (SystemStats). `screen: true` stages a whole screen (1066 x 600, no island ground) for the lock screen; a prop "@lock" is a stand-in lock in its resting state; `hide` names item types left out of the picture once it settles (the lock's clock digits: their line boxes overlap the date by design and are measured by clock-ground). `["@setting", key, value]` in `set` changes a setting for the scene and puts it back after.
